candidate_relations.reason: Malignant melanoma is the tumor family but omits that the enlarging pigmented plaque involves vermilion and intraoral mucosa.
Labial melanoma matches the 4-year pigmented vermilion plaque that began as a 1 cm macule and spawned multiple papules with adjacent cutaneous discoloration.
Angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia is a vascular eosinophilic proliferation, not a four-year pigmented ulcerating mucosal plaque.
Mucosal melanoma matches the progressive pigmented vermilion-to-intraoral lesion with focal ulceration.
Keratoacanthoma is a keratinizing crateriform nodule, not a slowly expanding pigmented mucosal macule-to-papules plaque.
Labial lentigo maligna is a cutaneous sun-damaged in-situ pattern, whereas this lesion ulcerates across wet mucosa from the frenum.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: cutaneous in-situ LM vs mucosal melanoma

candidate_relations.reason: Traumatic tattoo does not slowly enlarge over four years or ulcerate the labial mucosa.
Oral pigmentation describes the color change but not the neoplastic mucosal melanoma.
A simple lentigo would remain a stable macule, not spawn multiple papules, swelling, and intraoral ulceration.
Lip melanoma is the same mucosal melanoma of the upper-left vermilion with contiguous intraoral spread.
A melanocytic nevus should not progressively enlarge for years with mucosal ulceration and cutaneous spillover.
Laugier–Hunziker syndrome produces benign multifocal macules, not a solitary expanding ulcerated labial-intraoral tumor.
Kaposi sarcoma is not suggested in an otherwise healthy driver with a pigmented vermilion plaque and normal blood counts.
Hemangioma is a vascular lesion, not a brown-black progressive mucosal plaque.
Melanoma is the parent malignancy and still omits the required mucosal (vermilion-intraoral) site.
Leukoplakia is a white keratotic plaque, opposite the documented brown-black pigmentation.
Lip nevus is a benign melanocytic lesion and conflicts with ulcerated intraoral extension of a growing pigmented plaque.
Peutz–Jeghers is unsupported: no family history, no other mucocutaneous spots, and a single progressive ulcerating lesion.
A labial melanotic macule remains flat and small, unlike this 4-year enlarging papular plaque with intraoral ulceration.
Oral melanosis is benign mucosal pigment and does not produce swelling, papules, and focal ulceration.

case_quality_flags: No histopathology is provided; mucosal melanoma is inferred from a progressive pigmented vermilion-intraoral plaque with ulceration.
